meta.name: Starfall
meta.subtitle: Second city of the Noctari, seat of the Academy of Astral Harmony
meta.era: Part One — The Architect, c. 1450 AO (Age of Order, the city alive)
meta.culture: Noctari (night elf); Umbrion-aligned; scholars of the heavens
meta.coordinate_system: polar around the caldera centre (0,0). r = metres from centre; a_deg = degrees where 0 = +Z (front / the Grand Processional & causeway), increasing toward +X. world x = r*sin(a), z = r*cos(a). y = terrace top height (metres). Screen/plate angle = 180 - a_deg.
meta.status: FOUNDATION + two wedges fully specified (House Vael'Suran H0, House Serenthil H8 — the pair flanking the Grand Processional). Seven Houses + the Academy island still stubbed. Geometry LOCKED to godot/threed/StarfallCity3D.gd & docs/Scale_Reference.md.
meta.theme: Two maps of one city. The Plate (this visible survey) and the Ledger-map beneath it (the Under-Terraces) do not contain each other. That omission is the story of Part One.

grid.kind: metric survey grid overlaid on the radial city
grid.note: The city is radial (concentric caldera). The grid is a coordinate reference for placement, not a street grid — Starfall has no Cartesian blocks.

geometry_locked.note: Under-Terraces occupy negative Y beneath the shore/canal rings — the service city the Plate omits (barge locks, conduit galleries, bunk-halls). Depths -8 to -30.

districts.name: The Rim & the Nine Towers
districts.desc: The rim walk crowned by the nine House observatory towers (one dead). Each House seats itself here, highest and coldest, above its own wedge.

districts.name: The Upper Terraces
districts.desc: Sparse villas of senior astronomers, each with a surveyed, legally-protected sightline down to the Mirror (the 'ray-lines' of the Plate). To lose your sightline is to lose your rank.

districts.name: The Middle Terraces
districts.desc: Lecture annexes, scribe-halls, chart-makers and lens-guilds, and the dwellings of lesser scholars who serve the Houses without a sightline of their own.

districts.name: The Canal Quarter
districts.desc: The dense, warm, lowest visible ring: three star-water canals, footbridges, instrument-workshops, market rows, inns, a shrine. Where the city actually lives.

districts.name: The Shore & Processionals
districts.desc: Black basalt strand where the four processionals meet the star-lake; the armillary monument; customs posts where goods arrive from below.

districts.name: The Mirror & Causeway
districts.desc: The star-lake — a hole showing sky — crossed by the single railless causeway to the Academy island.

districts.name: The Academy of Astral Harmony (island)
districts.desc: Dead centre: the great observatory, theory wings, moon-bridge, the warded containment structure. Elorin, Corel, Coil, Sera and the Nullstone team work here.

districts.name: The Under-Terraces
districts.desc: THE OMITTED CITY. Beneath the canal quarter and shore: barge locks that raise cargo from the world below, conduit galleries carrying the Song to the star-lamps, bunk-halls of Terran deep-wrights and orc labour, the canteens and foremen. Not on the Plate. Not by conspiracy — the cartographers simply never considered it part of the city.

houses.name: House Vael'Suran
houses.domain: The unmoving stars; the master survey from which every sightline in Starfall is measured. The eldest and proudest House; its charts are the city's ground truth.
houses.sigil: a silver gnomon crossed by a single fixed star, on indigo
houses.colours: silver-white on deep indigo; a thread of antique gold

houses.name: House Nyx'Talar
houses.domain: Eclipses, transits, and every moment one light passes behind another. Readers of what hides what.
houses.sigil: a black disc crossing a silver ring

houses.name: House Oravelle
houses.domain: The wandering lights (planets); ephemerides and prediction. The House the Conclave trusts with dates.
houses.sigil: five linked circlets in a curve

houses.name: House Sabreth
houses.domain: Comets and omens; the House everyone consults and no one admits to consulting. Faintly disreputable, quietly wealthy.
houses.sigil: a silver star trailing a fine comet-tail of gold

houses.name: House Ilmyra
houses.epithet: Keepers of the Tides of the Song
houses.domain: The moons and the slow tides the Song makes in all things; the House that tends the city's water-clocks and the canal locks' timing.
houses.note: Its wedge holds the Grand Processional's far (-Z/back) counterpart is NOT here; the front processional falls in the Vael'Suran/Serenthil gap.

houses.name: House Corvane
houses.domain: The dark between the stars — the void itself. The most Umbrion-aligned House; feared a little, and the one whose theory feeds the Academy's void-work. Elorin's intellectual kin, though not her blood.
houses.sigil: an empty silver ring around unmarked indigo

houses.name: House ————
houses.domain: Unknown / struck from the record. Its dome is dark, its sigil scraped from the ring, its name unsaid. No one has ever proposed relighting it; some absences are load-bearing.
houses.sigil: none — a dome struck through with one black shard
houses.note: The dead House of the greybox (DEAD_TOWER index). Its wedge is the city's quiet scar — under-tended terraces, cheaper rents, the district people move to when they wish not to be measured.

houses.name: House Duskmere
houses.domain: The twilight band, risings and settings, the last and first light. The House of thresholds and departures; keeps the outer switchback stair and the rim gates.
houses.sigil: a silver line of horizon under a half-sunk star

houses.name: House Serenthil
houses.domain: The meridian and the hour; timekeepers of Starfall. They ring the bells, including the ninth-bell count of every Luminarae — and the same bells that toll the festival toll the labour-shifts in the dark below. The House the whole city depends on and none reveres: a utility, not a glory. Flanks the Grand Processional opposite Vael'Suran.
houses.sigil: a vertical silver meridian line through a single gold point
houses.colours: silver on indigo; one gold point at the meridian; verdigris on the bells

structures.name: The Gnomon Tower

position.note: the Vael'Suran rim observatory — greybox tower i=0

structures.purpose: The master survey of the fixed stars is kept and corrected here; every protected sightline in Starfall is a copy of a line first drawn in this tower. The House's authority is literally the instrument on its top floor.

rooms.name: The Meridian Hall
rooms.purpose: ground instrument hall; the great mural quadrant fixed to the north wall

rooms.name: The Chart Vault
rooms.purpose: fireproof silver-lined vault of the master plates; only the House head and First Surveyor hold keys

rooms.name: Head's Study
rooms.purpose: Magister Ysolde's study, sightline due to the Mirror

rooms.name: Computers' Room
rooms.purpose: where junior scholars reduce the night's readings by hand; ink, tables, and quiet

rooms.name: The Gnomon Chamber
rooms.purpose: top floor; the great gnomon and the roof aperture; the reading is taken standing in the cold

rooms.name: Servants' stair & lamp-room
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the star-lamp that crowns the dome is tended from here

structures.notes: 3 named + 4 live-in junior computers (dormitory on the 4th floor). The dome's lit finial is one of the nine on the greybox rim.

structures.name: The Vael'Suran Seat
structures.purpose: The living seat of the House on the rim beside its tower — cold, immaculate, and arranged so that every principal room holds the same framed view of the star-lake. Status here is measured in windows.

rooms.name: The Hall of Sightlines
rooms.purpose: reception; nine framed sightline-drawings, one per generation of heads

rooms.name: Ysolde's chambers
rooms.purpose: the matriarch's rooms, the best sightline in the House

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: four chambers for the near family

rooms.name: Cold-court
rooms.purpose: an open inner court left deliberately unroofed to the sky — the House takes readings without leaving home

rooms.name: Kitchen & stores
rooms.purpose: below the hall

rooms.name: Staff quarters
rooms.purpose: attic rooms for the household staff

structures.notes: Ysolde + near family (5) + 13 household staff (cook, chart-porters, lamp-tender, a gate-lodge keeper, maids). Ysolde also keeps a study in the tower.

structures.name: The Corrected Chart (the Open House)

position.note: the enterable interior already built in godot/threed/StarfallCity3D.gd (_build_open_house)

structures.purpose: Home and working room of Sub-Magister Aeliston Vael'Suran, a cousin of the House who keeps the running correction of the caldera's own sky from this terrace. A lifetime's chart is pinned to the lectern, corrected in a fine hand.

rooms.name: The Reading Room
rooms.purpose: one open room; the star-chart lectern against the back wall, a cot, a stove, a cold-shelf of instruments

structures.notes: Ties the built Open House interior into canon. Aeliston lives alone by choice; the whole House thinks him eccentric for keeping his own hours and his own door.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — Halvenor
structures.purpose: The household of First Surveyor Halvenor Daskei, the House's most important commoner-born scholar — the man who actually runs the survey Ysolde signs.

rooms.name: Ground hall & study
rooms.purpose: study with the protected sightline; a second-best mural quadrant

rooms.name: Family rooms (x3)
rooms.purpose: Halvenor, his wife, three children

rooms.name: Roof platform
rooms.purpose: a private observing platform — the perquisite of his post

structures.notes: Halvenor (First Surveyor), spouse Renne, 3 children, 1 live-in aunt.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — Corvane-in-marriage
structures.purpose: A Vael'Suran daughter married into House Corvane (the Deep Field) and kept her sightline; the villa quietly does void-adjacent work the fixed-star House disowns in public and funds in private.

rooms.name: Study of the Dark
rooms.purpose: shuttered by day; the sightline used at new-moon only

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the couple + 2 children

rooms.name: Servant's room
rooms.purpose: one maid

structures.notes: Magistra Ivrenne (née Vael'Suran) + husband + 2 children + 1 maid. A thread that connects wedge 0 to House Corvane (H5).

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Widow Sarrent
structures.purpose: A villa whose sightline is being slowly, legally encroached by a neighbour's new roofline — the great terror of the upper terrace. The widowed astronomer Sarrent is fighting it in the House court and losing.

rooms.name: Contested study
rooms.purpose: the sightline here is 4 degrees narrower than it was a decade ago

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: Sarrent + a companion

structures.notes: Sarrent + companion Ol + one servant. A ready side-quest seed (the sightline suit).

structures.name: The Scribes' Hall of the Fixed Stars
structures.purpose: Where the House's charts are fair-copied and bound, and where the apprentice scribes lodge. A young Noctari apprentice named Talindir keeps a cot and a candle here — he is eighty, which for an elf is a boy, and he copies faster and more beautifully than anyone will admit.

rooms.name: The Copying Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked sloped desks under high comb-crystal windows

rooms.name: The Binding Room
rooms.purpose: presses, thread, silver leaf

rooms.name: Apprentices' dormitory
rooms.purpose: 12 cots; Talindir's is by the window

rooms.name: Master-scribe's room
rooms.purpose: the hall's warden

structures.notes: Master-scribe Ovinn + 13 apprentices incl. Talindir (CH-006, here as an apprentice ~1450 AO — 550 years before the Cold Open). Canonical anchor.

structures.name: The Lens-Grinders' Court
structures.purpose: Optical glass for the whole wedge is ground and figured here — the slow, wet, patient trade that makes the Houses' instruments possible and gets none of the credit. A family firm, three generations deep.

rooms.name: The Grinding Shed
rooms.purpose: pitch laps, abrasive tubs, the great figuring wheel

rooms.name: The Testing Room
rooms.purpose: a dark room with a slit; lenses proved against a star-lamp

rooms.name: Family dwelling
rooms.purpose: the Marn family above the shed

rooms.name: The Court
rooms.purpose: open drying/working court

structures.notes: Master optician Delu Marn + spouse + 4 children + 3 journeymen (lodged).

structures.name: Lesser Scholars' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined narrow houses of the wedge's lesser scholars — the reducers, correctors, and lecture-assistants who serve the Houses without a sightline of their own. Respectable, cramped, sightless.

rooms.name: Per-house: ground room + 2 up
rooms.purpose: each of the 6 houses: a work-room and two small chambers

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls total (the reducer Kessa Von and family named; the rest counted). No protected sightline — a social border made of geometry.

structures.name: The Sounding-Glass
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, on the canal — warm, low-ceilinged, loud, and the one place a sightless scholar, an off-shift deep-wright, and a slumming House son drink in the same room. In game terms, the Strain-relief haven for this quarter (Zone_Atlas Z-06).

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, the cracked sounding-glass over the bar that gives the place its name

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above for travellers and the newly-evicted

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: canal-cooled store; a hatch to the Under-Terraces the innkeeper pretends not to know about

structures.notes: Innkeeper Bruin Hale + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar hatch is a real connection to VS-X05 (a thing the Plate does not know).

structures.name: The Instrument Market
structures.purpose: Ten stalls and shopfronts: brass-founders, tube-makers, engravers of scales, a dealer in second-hand quadrants, a paper-and-ink merchant. Live-over-the-shop trade.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + workshop + room above
rooms.purpose: 10 units, most with a family living above

structures.notes: 10 shops, ~34 souls. Named: brass-founder Ossa Kellen (whose foundry vents to an Under-Terrace flue), engraver the elder Pim.

structures.name: The Deepening
structures.purpose: A small windowless shrine to Umbrion, Weaver of Shadow — dark on purpose, entered to sit in the friendly void the Noctari call presence, not absence. A keeper tends one silver lamp that is never lit.

rooms.name: The Dark Cell
rooms.purpose: no light; a bowl of still star-water; you find the seat by touch

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room

structures.notes: The keeper, blind Serae — chosen for the post because the dark costs her nothing. A quiet counterpoint to the Solari sun-worship of the Cold Open.

structures.name: Vara's Garret
structures.purpose: A single rented attic room where Vara — the human prodigy the Academy uses and under-credits — lives. Books to the ceiling, a borrowed quadrant she is not supposed to have, and the longest walk to the island of anyone on the team, because a human is not given rooms on the rim.

rooms.name: The Garret
rooms.purpose: bed, desk, and more paper than floor; a skylight she uses as a poor man's aperture

structures.notes: Vara (CH-010, PO-008) — canonical Nullstone-team anchor placed in wedge 0. 'Twice as good, half as credited' is literally spatial here: she has the worst room and the best mind in the wedge.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Lockside
structures.purpose: The densest housing on the visible city: eight dwellings stacked three storeys over the canal, home to the artisans, boatwrights, lamplighters and canal-workers who keep the quarter running.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~38 souls. Named: lamplighter Corrun, who climbs the whole wedge every dusk, and knows a stair down that isn't drawn.

structures.name: The Vael'Suran Canal & its two bridges

position.note: one of the greybox's three canals, threading the wedge's canal quarter

footprint.form: curved channel, base_a ~0.35 rad in greybox

structures.purpose: Star-water — black, still, faintly starred — runs the canal that both drains the quarter and, through the lock below, connects to the barges of the Under-Terraces. Two arched stone footbridges cross it.
structures.notes: The canal is the visible top of an invisible system: what looks like a decorative channel is the throat of the cargo route the Plate omits (see VS-X01, the lock).

structures.name: The Processional Foot & Customs Post
structures.purpose: Where the Grand Processional meets the shore on the wedge's side: a customs post that weighs and tallies everything coming up from below before it is allowed onto the terraces. The one official door between the two cities — and it faces up, never down.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, a wardsealed strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs officer and two clerks

structures.notes: Customs officer Trell + 2 clerks (day post, not resident overnight — counted at their canal homes; listed here as workplace).

structures.name: Cael's Lock
structures.purpose: A stone chamber-lock that raises cargo barges from the world below the caldera up into the wedge's canal. The whole visible quarter's stone, glass, food and fuel arrives through here, lifted by chain-gangs. The Plate draws the pretty canal above it and stops.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding/emptying basin; the great counter-weighted gates

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: where the lift-gangs walk the capstans; named for a worker who died at them

rooms.name: Tally hole
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Named: lock-master Dregg. The under-clerk here keeps the OTHER tally — the real one, on ledger-paper, in charcoal.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery
structures.purpose: The Song does not fill the wedge's star-lamps by magic that tends itself. It is carried up this gallery in tuned crystal conduits that must be kept clean, aligned, and singing — hand-work, done in the dark, by people the light above never sees. When a lamp on the terrace 'simply burns,' someone down here made it.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; access ladders up to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where conduit-wrights kneel to true the crystal

structures.notes: Worked by conduit-wrights (mostly Terran). Thematically the literal machinery behind the Cold Open's 'the star-lamps burn without flame because the Song fills them.'

structures.name: The Deep-Wrights' Hall
structures.purpose: Home and hall of the Terran stone-wrights who cut and maintain the Under-Terraces — the deep folk who literally hold the beautiful city up. Carved, warm with glow-stone, and prouder than anything on the rim. Durak Ironthought, the geomancer the Academy consults and the Houses condescend to, lodges here among his own kind when he is in Starfall.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a long stone table; the deep-folk do not build separate boxes to eat in

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~40 wrights

rooms.name: Durak's cell
rooms.purpose: a plain stone room; a geomancer's tuning-forks and a basin of still water

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine — the wrong god for this city, kept anyway

structures.notes: Durak Ironthought (CH-011, PO-009) + ~43 Terran deep-wrights. Canonical anchor; explains why Durak argues 'we would build a basin' — he lives with the people who build.

structures.name: The Lift-Gang Bunks
structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the orc lift-gangs who walk the lock capstans and carry what the barges bring. This is where the young Elorin, come down on some errand of theory, first SEES the labour the Academy is built on — the beat the Narrative Outline gives Ch2. Cruelty here is not spectacle; it is routine, and the routine is the point.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: riveted double-bunks for ~30; no window, because there is no outside to have one onto

rooms.name: The Collar-room
rooms.purpose: where shift-tallies are logged; a quiet, bureaucratic horror

structures.notes: ~30 orc labourers. Named: the elder Ghesh, who counts. Foreshadows Part Two's Ashpile without stating it. Part of the unnamed 778 the whole game is about.

structures.name: The Underspill Canteen

position.depth_note: at the junction of the galleries

structures.purpose: The one warm shared room of the Under-Terraces: a canteen at the crossing of the galleries where deep-wrights, lift-gangs, conduit-crews and the occasional lost scholar eat the same grey, good stew. The real social heart of the wedge — the thing the Plate has no symbol for.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestle tables, a great range, a wall where the dead are chalked

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the canteen-keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Mother Vesh + 3 helpers (resident in a back nook). The cellar hatch of the Sounding-Glass (VS-K01) comes out near here — the only informal seam between the two cities.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the customs stair

structures.purpose: A small hard office at the foot of the stair up to the customs post — the point where the under-city answers to the over-city. The foreman is the only person who routinely crosses between the two maps, and is trusted by neither.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, a locked shift-book

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Adric — over-city clothes, under-city hands. A natural quest-broker character.

structures.name: The Meridian Tower

position.note: the Serenthil rim tower — greybox tower i=8; the city's public timepiece, not a private observatory

structures.purpose: Where Starfall's time is made and rung. Not a House hiding its instrument but a House whose instrument the whole city can hear — the nine bells that mark the hours, the ceremonies, and (a fact the rim prefers not to dwell on) the labour-shifts below. Vael'Suran keeps the eye; Serenthil keeps the ear.

rooms.name: The Bell-Chamber
rooms.purpose: the nine verdigris bells in their frame; the ninth is the great one, rung only at the solstice count

rooms.name: The Clockwork Hall
rooms.purpose: the master escapement driven by star-water from the cistern below; a floor of turning brass

rooms.name: The Meridian Slit
rooms.purpose: a north-south roof-slit; noon is the instant a fixed star crosses it — time proved against the sky

rooms.name: Strike-Master's watch-room
rooms.purpose: someone watches the clock every hour of every night; the post is never empty

rooms.name: Ringers' loft & rope-race
rooms.purpose: the ropes drop from here — some to the belfry, some straight down into the dark to the shift-bells

structures.notes: Head + Strike-Master + 4 live-in ringers/watch-keepers. Its lit finial is one of the greybox's nine rim domes.

structures.name: The Serenthil Seat
structures.purpose: Plainer than Vael'Suran's Seat and closer to the street — Serenthil money is civic money, made from keeping everyone's time, and the House wears its usefulness where the fixed-star grandees wear their view. Every room is on time; not one clock in it agrees to be wrong.

rooms.name: The Striking Hall
rooms.purpose: reception; a wall of the House's retired clocks, each stopped at the hour of a death

rooms.name: Head's chambers
rooms.purpose: Magister Toll Serenthil's rooms

rooms.name: Family & apprentice rooms
rooms.purpose: family + two horology apprentices boarded in

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff
rooms.purpose: household below and attic

structures.notes: Toll + family (5) + 2 boarded apprentices + 11 staff. Less grand, more lived-in than VS-M01.

structures.name: The Strike-Master's Villa
structures.purpose: Home of the Strike-Master, the commoner-born officer who actually decides when the bells ring — a heavier hand on the city's day than most House heads. His sightline matters less to him than his hearing-line: he can tell a mistuned bell from three terraces off.

rooms.name: The Listening Room
rooms.purpose: shuttered, bare, acoustically true; he checks the bells' pitch from here

rooms.name: Family rooms (x3)
rooms.purpose: the Strike-Master, spouse, 3 children

structures.notes: Strike-Master Venn Ostreth + household.

structures.name: The Horologist's Villa
structures.purpose: The villa of the House's chief horologist — the theorist of time itself, who argues that the Song has a beat and that a perfect clock would simply count it. Half the Academy thinks him a crank; the other half quietly borrows his figures.

rooms.name: The Escapement Study
rooms.purpose: a study full of half-built regulators, each trying to find the Song's beat

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the horologist + a companion + one apprentice

structures.notes: Chief horologist Marn Ilve + household. Provides a theory-thread toward the Academy's Song-work.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Quiet House
structures.purpose: A Serenthil villa let, unusually, to a tenant from outside the House — an aged Noctari astronomer who wanted only quiet and a view, and pays for both. The House takes the coin and pretends the arrangement is temporary; it has been temporary for ninety years.

rooms.name: The Study
rooms.purpose: an outsider's sightline, rented

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: the tenant + a single servant

structures.notes: Tenant-astronomer Ollisan + 4 (companion, servant, 2 boarders). A wedge with rented rooms reads differently from Vael'Suran's closed bloodline.

structures.name: The Bell-Foundry
structures.purpose: Loud, hot, and the opposite of everything the rim pretends to be: the wedge's bells and clock-brass are cast and tuned here. A bell is tuned by shaving metal from its inside until its note is true — a craft of subtraction, done by ear, over weeks. The most important trade in Serenthil and the least gentrified.

rooms.name: The Casting Floor
rooms.purpose: the bell-pit, the furnace, the crane; a floor no scholar visits twice

rooms.name: The Tuning Bay
rooms.purpose: where a cast bell is shaved to its true note against a monochord

rooms.name: Founders' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the master founder's family above the heat

rooms.name: Journeymen's loft
rooms.purpose: boarded workers

structures.notes: Master founder Hessa Drun + family + 8 journeymen. The vent-flue drops to the under-forge (SR-X04).

structures.name: The Horologists' Hall
structures.purpose: The clockmakers: escapement-fitters, gear-cutters, dial-engravers, and the water-clock wrights who keep the city's public clepsydrae running. Fine, patient, indoor work — the bench-craft that turns the founder's raw brass into time.

rooms.name: The Bench Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked benches under north light; a wall of running regulators for comparison

rooms.name: The Wheel-Cutting Room
rooms.purpose: the dividing engine that cuts gear-teeth — the Hall's guarded secret

rooms.name: Apprentices' dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded apprentices

structures.notes: Guild-warden Pel Corriden + 8 (fitters & apprentices).

structures.name: Lesser Timekeepers' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's lesser timekeepers — the hour-callers, dial-readers, water-tenders and rope-boys who serve the Tower without ever entering the bell-chamber. Respectable, sightless, and paid in the House's steady, unglamorous coin.

rooms.name: Per-house: work-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 6 households

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls. Named: hour-caller old Renn, whose voice the whole wedge wakes to.

structures.name: The Ninth Bell
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, named for the great solstice bell you can feel in your chest from here — and the one place the day's timekeeping stops mattering. Rope-boys, off-shift founders, and the occasional deaf old ringer drink under a cracked bell hung over the bar. This wedge's Strain-relief haven.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, the cracked bell; a clock deliberately kept five minutes wrong, as a joke that is also a mercy

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: a canal-cooled store; a grille here opens onto the shift-bell undercroft — you hear the dark ringing through it

structures.notes: Innkeeper Wenna Kob + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar grille is Serenthil's over/under seam (to SR-X01).

structures.name: The Clepsydra-Works
structures.purpose: The public water-clocks of the whole city are built and regulated here, tapping the canal's star-water — the works that turns flowing water into counted time. A calm, dripping, faintly hypnotic place; its overflow feeds back to the canal, and its intake comes up from the Great Cistern below.

rooms.name: The Flow Hall
rooms.purpose: tiered basins, float-gauges, the master clepsydra whose drip sets the Tower's water-drive

rooms.name: The Regulator Room
rooms.purpose: where flow is trimmed to a true hour

rooms.name: Wrights' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the water-wrights above

structures.notes: Water-warden Iss Vellun + 11 (wrights & families). Mechanically ties the canal, the cistern and the Tower into one water-driven clock.

structures.name: Sera's Lodging
structures.purpose: Two small rented rooms where Sera lodges — a Solari structural enchantress, a sun-elf alone in the night-city, on the Nullstone team and trusted by no faction on it. She chose the timekeepers' wedge on purpose: their bells are the one thing in Starfall that keep to a schedule she recognises, and she keeps a single forbidden sun-lamp she lights only when the shutters are closed.

rooms.name: Work-room
rooms.purpose: structural models in silver wire; a Solari sun-disc turned to the wall

rooms.name: Sleeping room
rooms.purpose: a cot, a shuttered window, the sun-lamp

structures.notes: Sera (CH-008, PO-006) — 'the outsider's outsider.' Canonical Nullstone-team anchor in this wedge, deliberately mirroring Vara's garret in the Vael'Suran wedge.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Watergate
structures.purpose: Dense canalside housing by the watergate, home to the rope-boys, water-tenders, dial-runners and canal-hands who keep the wedge's time-machinery fed and moving. The block wakes to old Renn's hour-call and sleeps to the ninth-of-night bell.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~40 souls. Named: the widow Ferrun, whose late husband fell from the belfry, and who counts every bell since.

structures.name: The Hour-Market
structures.purpose: A market that opens and closes to the bell — nine stalls and shops selling by strict tolled hours (a Serenthil custom, and a small tyranny): a baker, a dial-shop, a candle-and-oil merchant, a rope-walk, a cook-stall, a scrivener, a herbalist. Live-over-the-shop trade timed to the death by the very House that sells them the clocks.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + room above
rooms.purpose: 9 units, most with a family above

structures.notes: 9 shops, ~22 souls. Named: the baker Doln, who bribes a rope-boy to ring his opening a half-minute early.

structures.name: The Bell-Gate & Processional Foot
structures.purpose: Where the Grand Processional meets the shore on Serenthil's side: a gate with its own small bell that opens and closes the processional to ceremony, and a customs post twinned with Vael'Suran's across the way. The two Houses' gate-bells answer each other across the stair — the city's front door, in stereo.

rooms.name: The Gate Hall
rooms.purpose: the gate-bell rope, a tally-desk, a warded night-strongroom

rooms.name: Gatekeepers' room
rooms.purpose: the gate-warden and a clerk

structures.notes: Gate-warden Ospren + clerk (day post; counted at their canal homes).

structures.name: The Shift-Bell Undercroft
structures.purpose: The dark twin of the bell-chamber. The same ropes that ring the festival's ninth bell drop through the whole city to here, where under-ringers pull the SHIFT-bells that govern the labour below — the cistern-gangs, the bell-wrights, the lift-crews. To the rim, the bell is glory; to the dark, the identical bell is a whip you can hear but not see. Serenthil rings both and calls it one service.

rooms.name: The Under-Belfry
rooms.purpose: the shift-bells and the drop-ropes; a board chalked with the shift-count

rooms.name: Under-ringers' bunk
rooms.purpose: the ringers live at their ropes; they have not seen a festival in years

structures.notes: Under-ringer crew (8). The Sounding-metaphor made literal: one bell, two meanings, and only the dark hears both. The Ninth Bell inn's cellar grille opens near here.

structures.name: The Clock-Water Gallery
structures.purpose: Twin runs in one gallery: the tuned Song-conduits that feed this wedge's star-lamps (as under Vael'Suran) AND the star-water race that carries the Great Cistern's water up to the clepsydra-works and the Tower's clock-drive. When a lamp burns or a clock ticks on the terraces above, its cause is in this tunnel, tended in the dark.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: conduit + water-race side by side; access ladders to each terrace

rooms.name: Sluice niches (x3)
rooms.purpose: where water-wrights set the race's flow

structures.notes: Conduit-and-race crew (6, mixed Terran & human). The literal plumbing of both light and time.

structures.name: The Great Cistern

position.depth_note: a vaulted reservoir deep under the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Starfall's hidden heart of star-water: a vast pillared vault of black, still, faintly-starred water that drives every clock, feeds every canal-lock, and cools the whole under-city — a subterranean night sky underneath the lake that is a night sky. The single most impressive space in Starfall, and it is on no map, because the people who need it are not on the map either. Reached by boat across its own black surface.

rooms.name: The Vault
rooms.purpose: forty stone pillars standing in still water; a rowed jetty; the water doubles the lamplight into a false depth

rooms.name: The Pump-Floor
rooms.purpose: the great treadwheel pumps that lift water to the race — walked by the cistern-gangs

rooms.name: Keepers' rooms
rooms.purpose: the cistern-keepers, who live beside the water and learn to read its level like a face

structures.notes: Cistern-keepers + pump-crew (12). The wedge's 'novel and unique' landmark — a cathedral of dark water no citizen above has ever seen. Strong future hero-set-piece.

structures.name: The Bell-Wrights' & Cistern-Gangs' Hall
structures.purpose: The largest under-dwelling of the wedge: Terran bell-wrights (who tune the shift-bells and cast the clock-brass at an under-forge the foundry's flue feeds) alongside the human and orc cistern-gangs who walk the pumps. A rare mixed hall — the Song does not reach here, so the races that the city above keeps carefully apart share one warm, loud, glow-lit room.

rooms.name: The Under-Forge
rooms.purpose: a small casting floor fed by the Bell-Foundry's flue; shift-bells are born and tuned here

rooms.name: The Long Hall
rooms.purpose: shared eating-and-living hall; a Petrocore shrine and a scratched orc tally-board share a wall

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~46 wrights and gang-hands

structures.notes: ~30 Terran bell-wrights + ~16 human/orc cistern-gang. The mixed hall varies the texture from Vael'Suran's segregated Terran/orc halls, and is a natural place for a cross-race scene.

structures.name: The Undertoll Canteen
structures.purpose: The under-city's warm room for this wedge, named for the toll-bell that calls its meal-shifts. Under-ringers, cistern-gangs, bell-wrights and conduit-crews eat here between shifts; the canteen-keeper rings her own small bell for meals and, once a year, quietly rings it nine times for the dead.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall of chalked names

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Old Sable + 3 helpers. Sister-room to Vael'Suran's Underspill; the two under-canteens know each other's runners.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the bell-gate stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office of Serenthil's under-city, at the foot of the stair up to the Bell-Gate — where the shift-count is reconciled against the toll and sent up to the House. The foreman keeps time for people the timekeepers never count.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a shift-book, a small answering bell wired to the undercroft

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Quill — keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's count in ink, and knows they differ.

npcs.name: Magister Ysolde Vael'Suran
npcs.role: Head of House Vael'Suran; Keeper of the Master Survey
npcs.note: Ancient, exact, proud; signs the survey her First Surveyor actually runs. The city's sightlines are her family's word made law.

npcs.name: First Reader Pan-Ostrel
npcs.role: senior observer, the Gnomon Chamber
npcs.note: Takes the cold midnight readings; they and the gnomon are the only two things in the House never wrong.

npcs.name: the junior computers (4)
npcs.role: live-in calculating clerks
npcs.note: Reduce the night's numbers by hand; dream in tables.

npcs.name: Ilvenor Vael'Suran
npcs.role: Ysolde's heir, bored and dangerous with it
npcs.note: Slums at the Sounding-Glass; will inherit sightlines he has never once looked along.

npcs.name: the near family (3)
npcs.role: House family

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (13)
npcs.role: cook, chart-porters, lamp-tender, gate-keeper, maids
npcs.note: Includes two humans who may not dine in the rooms they clean.

npcs.name: Sub-Magister Aeliston Vael'Suran
npcs.role: cousin of the House; keeper of the running correction of the caldera's own sky
npcs.note: Lives alone with his door open; the Open House lectern is his life's chart. The eccentric the House indulges.

npcs.name: First Surveyor Halvenor Daskei
npcs.role: commoner-born scholar who actually runs the survey
npcs.note: The mind behind Ysolde's signature; keeps a private roof platform because the House will not give him a tower key.

npcs.name: Renne Daskei & 4 (family)
npcs.role: Halvenor's household

npcs.name: Magistra Ivrenne (née Vael'Suran, m. Corvane)
npcs.role: void-adjacent scholar; the House's disowned-and-funded research
npcs.note: Household of 5. A living link to House Corvane (H5).

npcs.name: Astronomer Sarrent
npcs.role: widowed scholar losing a sightline suit
npcs.note: Household of 3. Side-quest seed: the encroached sightline.

npcs.name: Master-scribe Ovinn
npcs.role: warden of the Scribes' Hall

npcs.name: Talindir
npcs.role: apprentice scribe, the fastest and finest hand in the hall
npcs.note: The Cold Open's chronicler, 550 years younger. Copies the fixed-star charts; observation is already 'the only thing he does well enough for it to constitute protection.'

npcs.name: Master optician Delu Marn + household (9)
npcs.role: lens-grinders

npcs.name: Lesser Scholars' Row (22)
npcs.role: reducers, correctors, lecture-assistants; sightless
npcs.note: Named principal: reducer Kessa Von. A social border made of geometry — no protected view.

npcs.name: Bruin Hale + house (5)
npcs.role: innkeeper of the Sounding-Glass
npcs.note: Knows about the cellar hatch to the under-city and says nothing.

npcs.name: The Instrument Market (34)
npcs.role: brass-founders, tube-makers, engravers, a paper merchant
npcs.note: Named: brass-founder Ossa Kellen; the elder engraver Pim.

npcs.name: Serae the shrine-keeper
npcs.role: keeper of the Deepening (Umbrion shrine)
npcs.note: Blind; chosen because the dark costs her nothing.

npcs.name: Vara
npcs.role: structural theorist on the Nullstone team; the wedge's best mind, worst room
npcs.note: 'Twice as good, half as credited.' A human housed in a canal garret while lesser Noctari keep rim villas; walks the whole city to the island every day.

npcs.name: Lockside dwellings (38)
npcs.role: artisans, boatwrights, lamplighters, canal-workers
npcs.note: Named: lamplighter Corrun, who knows a stair down that isn't drawn.

npcs.name: Customs officer Trell + 2 clerks
npcs.role: weighs everything that comes up from below
npcs.note: Guards the one official door between the two cities; it only faces up.

npcs.name: Lock-master Dregg
npcs.role: runs Cael's Lock
npcs.note: The under-clerk beneath him keeps the real ledger — the Other Map's tally.

npcs.name: Conduit-wrights (crew of 6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing up to the star-lamps
npcs.note: The literal hands behind 'the lamps simply burn.'

npcs.name: Durak Ironthought
npcs.role: geomancer; Nullstone-team consultant; lodges among the deep-wrights
npcs.note: 'You are trying to redirect water; we would build a basin.' He lives with the people who actually build — the whole reason he sees what the elves miss.

npcs.name: The Deep-Wrights (43)
npcs.role: cut and hold up the Under-Terraces
npcs.note: Proud, glow-stone-warm, prouder than the rim. Keep a shrine to Petrocore in a city of the wrong god.

npcs.name: The Lift-Gang (30) — elder Ghesh
npcs.role: walk the lock capstans; carry what the barges bring
npcs.note: Where Elorin first SEES the labour (Narrative Outline Ch2). Ghesh counts the shifts. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Mother Vesh + 3
npcs.role: canteen-keeper of the Underspill
npcs.note: Feeds every race in the under-city the same good grey stew; chalks the dead on the wall.

npcs.name: Foreman Adric
npcs.role: the seam between the two cities; answers to the over-city, works the under
npcs.note: Over-city clothes, under-city hands; trusted by neither map. Natural quest-broker.

npcs.name: Magister Toll Serenthil
npcs.role: Head of House Serenthil; Keeper of the Meridian
npcs.note: Civic, dry, and quietly aware that his House's dignity rests on being useful rather than revered. Signs the city's time into law.

npcs.name: Strike-Master Venn Ostreth
npcs.role: commoner-born officer who decides when the bells ring
npcs.note: A heavier hand on the city's day than most House heads; can hear a mistuned bell three terraces off.

npcs.name: the Tower ringers & watch (4)
npcs.role: live-in bell-ringers and clock-watchers

npcs.name: the Serenthil family (5)
npcs.role: House family + 2 boarded horology apprentices

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (11)
npcs.role: cook, clock-keeper, porters, maids

npcs.name: Venn Ostreth's household (5)
npcs.role: the Strike-Master's spouse & 3 children
npcs.note: Listed with NPC-SR-002 who heads it.

npcs.name: Chief Horologist Marn Ilve
npcs.role: theorist of time; argues the Song has a beat a perfect clock would count
npcs.note: Household of 5. A theory-thread toward the Academy's Song-work; half-crank, half-borrowed-from.

npcs.name: Tenant-astronomer Ollisan
npcs.role: outside tenant of a Serenthil villa; wanted only quiet and a view
npcs.note: Household of 5 incl. boarders. 'Temporary' for ninety years — a rented villa reads differently from a bloodline seat.

npcs.name: Master founder Hessa Drun + household (14)
npcs.role: runs the Bell-Foundry; tunes bells by ear over weeks
npcs.note: Least gentrified, most essential trade in the wedge.

npcs.name: Guild-warden Pel Corriden + hall (9)
npcs.role: clockmakers' guild; keeps the dividing engine's secret

npcs.name: Lesser Timekeepers' Row (22) — hour-caller Renn
npcs.role: hour-callers, dial-readers, water-tenders, rope-boys
npcs.note: Sightless service class; old Renn's voice wakes the wedge.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Wenna Kob + house (5)
npcs.role: keeps The Ninth Bell
npcs.note: Keeps one clock deliberately five minutes wrong; knows about the cellar grille to the undercroft.

npcs.name: Water-warden Iss Vellun + works (12)
npcs.role: runs the Clepsydra-Works; regulates the city's water-clocks
npcs.note: The human node between canal, cistern and Tower — all one water-driven clock.

npcs.name: Sera
npcs.role: structural enchantress on the Nullstone team; a sun-elf alone in the night-city
npcs.note: 'The outsider's outsider.' Lodges in the timekeepers' wedge because the bells keep a schedule she recognises; a forbidden sun-lamp lit only behind shutters. Mirrors Vara's garret across the Processional.

npcs.name: Watergate dwellings (40) — the widow Ferrun
npcs.role: rope-boys, water-tenders, dial-runners, canal-hands
npcs.note: Ferrun counts every bell since her husband fell from the belfry.

npcs.name: The Hour-Market (22) — the baker Doln
npcs.role: baker, dial-shop, chandler, rope-walk, cook-stall, scrivener, herbalist
npcs.note: Trades by tolled hours; Doln bribes a rope-boy to ring his opening early.

npcs.name: Gate-warden Ospren + clerk
npcs.role: works the Bell-Gate; twin to Vael'Suran's customs across the stair
npcs.note: Day post; the two gate-bells answer each other across the Processional.

npcs.name: The Under-Ringers (8)
npcs.role: pull the shift-bells that govern the labour below
npcs.note: Live at their ropes; have not seen a festival in years. One bell, two meanings — they hear both.

npcs.name: The Conduit-and-Race Crew (6)
npcs.role: keep the Song-conduits and the clock-water race

npcs.name: The Cistern-Keepers & pump-crew (12) — keeper Mave
npcs.role: tend the Great Cistern; walk the treadwheel pumps; read the water-level like a face
npcs.note: Keeper Mave has lived beside the black water so long she navigates the vault in the dark.

npcs.name: The Bell-Wrights (30) — under-founder Kragg
npcs.role: cast and tune the shift-bells and clock-brass at the under-forge
npcs.note: Keep a Petrocore shrine beside the orc tally-board in a shared hall.

npcs.name: The Cistern-Gangs (16)
npcs.role: walk the pumps; haul; the muscle of the water-system
npcs.note: Share the mixed hall with the bell-wrights — a rare place the city's races live in one room. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Canteen-keeper Old Sable + 3
npcs.role: keeps the Undertoll Canteen
npcs.note: Rings her meal-bell nine times a year for the dead. Knows Mother Vesh (VS-X05) by their runners.

npcs.name: Foreman Quill
npcs.role: the seam of Serenthil's under-city; reconciles the shift-count to the toll
npcs.note: Keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's in ink, and knows they differ. Twin to Foreman Adric.

design_notes.tallies_are_computed: Population per wedge and per district is summed from each structure's resident_count by the generators — never hand-maintained here, so it cannot drift.
design_notes.over_under_balance: In a finished wedge the Under-Terraces should hold roughly as many souls as the visible quarter above — and appear on no official map. That imbalance in plain sight is the theme.
design_notes.distinct_wedges: Wedges must not read as clones. Vael'Suran = the eye, pride, protected sightlines, a closed bloodline. Serenthil = the ear, the hour, civic utility, rented rooms, a mixed under-city. Each further House should get its own social texture from its celestial domain.
